QuestionStmt.S: If $$f(x) = \begin{cases} mx + 1, & x \leq \frac{\pi}{2}, \\ \sin x + n, & x > \frac{\pi}{2}, \end{cases}$$ is continuous at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, ($m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$) then

Solution.S:
For $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, we must have:

$$\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^+} f(x)$$

$$\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^-} (mx + 1) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}^+} (\sin x + n)$$

$$m \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} + 1 = \sin \frac{\pi}{2} + n$$

$$\frac{m\pi}{2} + 1 = 1 + n$$

$$\frac{m\pi}{2} = n$$

Thus $n = \frac{m\pi}{2}$, which corresponds to option D.
